q: Oxidation numbers have a variety of uses in chemistry, from writing formulae to predicting properties of compounds and assisting in the _____ of oxidation-reduction reactions.
e: Oxidation numbers have a variety of uses in chemistry, from writing formulae to predicting properties of compounds and assisting in the balancing of oxidation-reduction reactions. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: The oxidation number (or oxidation state) of an atom can be _____.
e: The oxidation number (or oxidation state) of an atom can be zero, positive, or negative. Free elements are assigned oxidation number 0, whether the molecule is monoatomic or diatomic. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion.

q: All elements in their free state (uncombined with other elements) have an oxidation number of _____.
e: All elements in their free state (uncombined with other elements) have an oxidation number of zero. Free elements are assigned oxidation number 0, whether the molecule is monoatomic or diatomic. An uncombined element in its free state has oxidation number zero.

q: A positive oxidation number means the atom has _____ electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom.
e: A positive oxidation number means the atom has more electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: A negative oxidation number means the atom has _____ electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom.
e: A negative oxidation number means the atom has fewer electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: The oxidation number of an atom that has lost or gained electrons to form an ion is the same as the _____ of the ion.
e: The oxidation number of an atom that has lost or gained electrons to form an ion is the same as the atomic number of the ion. A positive oxidation number means that atom is assigned fewer electrons than the neutral atom. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion.

q: All elements regardless of whether they are monoatomic, diatomic or triatomic have an oxidation number of _____.
e: All elements regardless of whether they are monoatomic, diatomic or triatomic have an oxidation number of zero. Free elements are assigned oxidation number 0, whether the molecule is monoatomic or diatomic. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion.

q: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of the atoms in a neutral molecule is _____.
e: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of the atoms in a neutral molecule is equal to the charge. In a neutral molecule the oxidation numbers of all atoms add up to zero. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of the atoms in a polyatomic ion is equal to the _____ on the ion.
e: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of the atoms in a polyatomic ion is equal to the atomic number on the ion. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: The oxidation number of H is +1, except in metal hydrides, where it is _____.
e: The oxidation number of H is +1, except in metal hydrides, where it is -1. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: The oxidation number of O is -2, except in peroxides, where it is _____.
e: The oxidation number of O is -2, except in peroxides, where it is -1. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom. Oxygen is usually -2, except in peroxides (-1) and in OF2 (+2).

q: The oxidation number of O is +2 in the compound _____.
e: The oxidation number of O is +2 in the compound BaO_2. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom. Oxygen is usually -2, except in peroxides (-1) and in OF2 (+2).

q: Alkali metals in combined state have an oxidation number of _____.
e: Alkali metals in combined state have an oxidation number of +2. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Combined alkali metals have oxidation number +1. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: Alkaline earth metals in combined state have an oxidation number of _____.
e: Alkaline earth metals in combined state have an oxidation number of +1. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: The oxidation number of halogen in compounds (e.g., $BaCl_2$, $NaBr$, $KI$) is typically _____.
e: The oxidation number of halogen in compounds (e.g., BaCl_2, NaBr, KI) is typically 0. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: In interhalogen compounds (e.g., $BrF$, $IF_7$, $ClF_3$), the oxidation number of halogen is _____.
e: In interhalogen compounds (e.g., BrF, IF_7, ClF_3), the oxidation number of halogen is negative. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom. In an interhalogen compound the less electronegative halogen takes the positive oxidation number.

q: In covalent compounds, the negative oxidation number is assigned to the _____ atom.
e: In covalent compounds, the negative oxidation number is assigned to the less electronegative atom. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.

q: The oxidation number of sulphur in sulphuric acid ($H_2SO_4$) is _____.
e: The oxidation number of sulphur in sulphuric acid (H_2SO_4) is +2. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom. Concentrated sulphuric acid is a strong acid, a dehydrating agent and an oxidising agent.

q: The oxidation number of manganese in the permanganate ion ($MnO_4^-$) is _____.
e: The oxidation number of manganese in the permanganate ion (MnO_4^-) is +7. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: A positive oxidation number indicates the number of electrons _____ from a neutral atom.
e: A positive oxidation number indicates the number of electrons removed from a neutral atom. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: A negative oxidation number indicates the number of electrons _____ to a neutral atom.
e: A negative oxidation number indicates the number of electrons shared to a neutral atom. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: In $NaCl$, the oxidation number for the $Na^+$ ion is _____.
e: In NaCl, the oxidation number for the Na^+ ion is +1. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. In NaCl, sodium is +1 and chlorine is -1. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: In $LiH$, the oxidation number of H is _____.
e: In LiH, the oxidation number of H is 0. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: In $BaO_2$, the oxidation number of O is _____.
e: In BaO_2, the oxidation number of O is +1. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom. Oxygen is usually -2, except in peroxides (-1) and in OF2 (+2).

q: The metallic element in an ionic compound has a _____ oxidation number.
e: The metallic element in an ionic compound has a negative oxidation number. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.
